decision: No additional defensible learner novelty gap found. Pairing, joint graph/model marginalization, learned stochastic structure and averaging nonlinear predictions already have primary precedents. Own-versus-pooled NCNC remains an established-mechanism empirical test.

paper_records.title: Bayesian Graph Convolutional Neural Networks using Node Copying
paper_records.scope: §3 Methodology, §§3.1–3.2, Eqs. (3)–(7), Algorithm 1 and GCNN weight-inference discussion
paper_records.history_status: reused identity; fresh scoped primary reinspection
paper_records.closest_prior_role: Feature/label-conditioned correlated neighborhood replacement and conditional weight inference
primary_text_verified: A base classifier supplies predicted-label groups; each node samples a donor from its predicted group.
Node copying changes the neighborhood to the donor's observed neighborhood while keeping node features unchanged.
Graph inference depends on observed topology, features and training labels.
The prose and Algorithm 1 train a GCNN over each sampled graph and use MC dropout for its conditional weights.
The printed v1 prediction factors in Eqs. (6)–(7) use G_obs; this differs from BGCN's prediction on sampled G and is preserved as a scope caveat.
limits: Node classification and neighborhood copying, not private NCNC completion scorers.
Do not silently replace G_obs with sampled G in the printed predictive equations.
Conditional fitting is approximate, not proof of exact Bayesian calibration.
paper_records.adoption: Use as prior for task-conditioned graph uncertainty and correlated neighborhood alternatives; qualify the printed inference graph.

paper_records.title: Bayesian Graph Neural Networks with Adaptive Connection Sampling
paper_records.scope: §3 Graph DropConnect, §§3.1–3.2, and §4 Variational Beta-Bernoulli GDC, Eqs. (4)–(12); not §5 random-walk variant
paper_records.history_status: reused identity; fresh scoped primary reinspection of v1 (older packet inspected v3)
paper_records.closest_prior_role: Learned stochastic connection masks, effective edge-weight interpretation and factorized variational training
primary_text_verified: A mask has the same sparsity as the input adjacency, and the graph operator uses A times Z elementwise.
The paper interprets masked messages as edge-associated effective weight matrices.
§3.2 factorizes q(W,Z)=q(W)q(Z) and uses q(W)=delta(W-M), so this inspected construction does not preserve arbitrary posterior dependence between global model weights and masks.
§4 learns hierarchical beta-Bernoulli sampling rates alongside GNN parameters, with Kumaraswamy variational rates and either relaxed gradients or ARM.
limits: Observed-edge masking cannot add a missing edge where input A is zero.
The variational family is factorized and the global model-weight distribution is a point mass in the inspected formulation.
§5 local random-walk masking and complete predictive-uncertainty implementation were not freshly read; prior packet is separately cited.
paper_records.adoption: Do not present learned mask/model training or edge-associated stochastic weights as new; do not equate these masks with NCNC missing-edge completion.

paper_records.title: CORE: Data Augmentation for Link Prediction via Information Bottleneck
paper_records.scope: §3 Proposed framework, §§3.1–3.4 including theorem statement; Appendix B.2–B.4; no proof audit
paper_records.history_status: new identity after searches of v33 and saved conclusion/report corpus
paper_records.closest_prior_role: Missing-edge inflation, learned target-link-specific stochastic reduction, shared encoder and nonlinear link prediction
primary_text_verified: Complete scores candidate nonedges with at least one common neighbor, adds top-k edges, and keeps inflated edges out of training labels.
Reduce conditions edge sampling probabilities on edge representation and target-link subgraph pooling; Bernoulli/Gumbel sampling trains a nonlinear subgraph predictor.
Predictor and reducer can share the same GNN encoder; completion-origin features and score buckets inform added-edge use.
Appendix B.3 explicitly uses expected edge probabilities as inference weights, rather than sampled graph prediction averaging.
Theorem 1 assumes a deterministic invertible local-neighborhood-to-link-probability mapping and coverage of that neighborhood by the inflated graph; its proof was not audited.
limits: A learned stochastic data augmentation/reduction law, not an exact joint completion/decoder Bayesian posterior.
Its native mean-weight inference is a comparator, not evidence that sampled inference improves quality.
No factorized decoder ensemble or persistent pairing of independent completion/head members is specified in the read method.
The 2026 journal DOI record and 2024 arXiv preprint are title/author-matched metadata; journal method changes were not inspected.
paper_records.adoption: Add a scoped learned-completion/link-decoding prior. Use expected-weight inference as a competent scope-specific comparator only if future work is authorized.
